about: What the droids say among themselves about the player, on every map: news of what the player did, and what they think of them (see hydroxus-ai's social::rumour and social::chat). Two droids that meet, or a group that talks among itself, near the player, talk of news one of them has and another has not, if any of them has some: the one that knows says one of 'news' for the deed - 'saw' if it saw it done itself, 'heard' if it was told - the other answers with one of 'reactions' for how it takes the player now it has heard it, and the first closes with one of 'closings'. With no news, one that feels strongly about the player says one of 'opinions' for how it takes them, and the other answers. Otherwise they have one of the script's own meetings or talks. A droid that hates the player will not talk to them, and says one of 'refusals' instead. Every 'says' is in System Latin, checked with data/system_latin/sl_parser.py; 'means' is the English under it.

saw.means: I saw the attacker. It shot a citizen down.
I saw it myself. The hostile shot a unit down.

heard.means: I got a report. An attacker shot a citizen down.
Unconfirmed: a hostile shot a unit down.

saw.means: I saw the thief, in a store.
I saw a robbery. The thief got away.

heard.means: I got a report. A bank was robbed.

saw.means: I saw a weapon pointed at a citizen.
A threat, seen. A weapon on a citizen.

heard.means: I got a report. A citizen was threatened.

friendly.means: Hard to believe. It's not hostile.
I doubt it. That's not confirmed.
I doubt it. It's not dangerous.

hostile.means: An enemy. If I see it, I sound the alarm.

hostile.says: Ille hostis. Si detectum, tunc sirena.
hostile.means: It's an enemy. If I see it, I sound the alarm.
